newsitem.title: USA: States see shift to third-party welfare providers.
newsitem.headline: States see shift to third-party welfare providers.

text.p: State welfare agency leaders expect their role to change from direct providers of services to arrangers of third-party services over the next five years, according to a survey released Tuesday by Andersen Consulting.

In a survey of 151 human services agency officials from 49 states, 52 percent said their organizations currently provide services such as job training, job placement and child care. But only 27 percent said they expect to do so five years from now. Fifty-eight percent predicted they will assume a more supervisory role.

They said private and third-party providers such as churches, synagogues and short-term food and shelter organizations are often closer to the community than government, and can provide better, more efficient services.

Forty percent said their agencies were ill prepared to handle greater responsibility for welfare-to-work programs, mostly because of inadequate funding, inefficient infrastructures or inadequate staff training.

But most said their states did not wait for Congress to enact welfare reform before embarking on some sort of change. Seventy-five percent said they were redesigning programs and processes while 79 percent were updating or integrating computer systems to better share information between agencies.

Research was conducted by Wirthlin Worldwide via telephone interviews with 151 directors or higher-level officials at state agencies that provide health, child and family services, welfare and food assistance, employment, training, human resources and employment security.
